summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and cirrhosis was readmitted six days after a prior discharge due to recurrent fevers, right upper quadrant pain, and nausea while on outpatient ertapenem for presumed cholangitis. Despite negative blood and urine cultures and no evidence of biliary obstruction on imaging, she was treated initially with meropenem and later daptomycin due to persistent fevers. After failing to respond to antibiotics and remaining afebrile off treatment, all antibiotics were discontinued. An ERCP showed chronic biliary narrowing consistent with PSC, and balloon dilation was performed. Diuretics were held initially but resumed when stable. She remained afebrile, and was discharged home with instructions to avoid antibiotics in the ED without consulting the liver team and to follow up for a repeat CT scan of a 5 mm lung nodule in one year.
